/journal/apprenticeship/.description: Apprenticed to James Basire, engraver to the Society of Antiquaries.
/journal/apprenticeship/.preview: On the fourth of August, in the year 1772, I was bound apprentice to Mr. James Basire, Engraver, of No. 31, Great Queen Street, Lincoln's Inn Fields, for the term of seven years.
/journal/apprenticeship/.title: The Apprentice Years

/journal/i-shant-live-five-years/.preview: I say I shan't live five years. And if I live one it will be a Wonder.
/journal/i-shant-live-five-years/.title: I Say I Shan't Live Five Years

/journal/marriage/.description: I married Catherine Boucher at St. Mary's, Battersea.
/journal/marriage/.preview: On the eighteenth of August I married Catherine Boucher at the church of St. Mary, Battersea. She is the daughter of a market-gardener. When I first told her of my love, she pitied me — and I knew then that she was the woman for me, for Pity divides the soul.
/journal/marriage/.title: Catherine

/journal/notebook-poems/.description: Poems not yet engraved. From the notebook at Hercules Buildings.
/journal/notebook-poems/.preview: These verses I have set down in my notebook but not yet committed to copper. Some may find their way into future works; others are for my eyes alone. I record them here as they came to me.
/journal/notebook-poems/.title: Poems from My Notebook

/journal/on-lavater/.description: Marginalia on J.C. Lavater's Aphorisms on Man, translated by Henry Fuseli.
/journal/on-lavater/.preview: I have read Lavater's Aphorisms on Man with attention, and find in many of them the voice of true wisdom — and in others, the voice of a man who mistakes prudence for virtue.
/journal/on-lavater/.title: Annotations on Lavater

/journal/on-reynolds/.description: Marginalia on Sir Joshua Reynolds' Discourses on Art.
/journal/on-reynolds/.preview: This Man was Hired to Depress Art. This is the opinion of Will Blake.
/journal/on-reynolds/.title: Annotations on Reynolds

/journal/on-swedenborg/.description: Marginalia on Swedenborg's Divine Love and Divine Wisdom.
/journal/on-swedenborg/.preview: I was once a follower of Swedenborg. Catherine and I signed the register of the New Church in April of eighty-nine. We believed then that he had seen Heaven and conversed with Angels.
/journal/on-swedenborg/.title: Annotations on Swedenborg

/journal/prospectus/.preview: The Labours of the Artist, the Poet, the Musician, have been proverbially attended by poverty and obscurity; this was never the fault of the Public, but was owing to a neglect of means to propagate such works as have wholly absorbed the Man of Genius. Even Milton and Shakespeare could not publish...
/journal/prospectus/.title: To the Public

/journal/the-ancients/.description: A circle of young men who call themselves the Ancients.
/journal/the-ancients/.preview: A circle of young men has formed around me in these last years. They call themselves the Ancients. Samuel Palmer, George Richmond, Edward Calvert, Frederick Tatham — they come to my rooms at Fountain Court and sit at my feet as if I were a prophet returned from the wilderness.
/journal/the-ancients/.title: The Ancients

/journal/the-bastille/.preview: The Bastille is fallen. The prisoners are free. I wear the red cap in the streets of London and am not ashamed.
/journal/the-bastille/.title: The Bastille

/journal/the-exhibition/.description: An exhibition of paintings at No. 28, corner of Broad Street, Golden Square.
/journal/the-exhibition/.preview: The execution of my Designs, being all in Water-colours, (that is in Fresco) are regularly refused to be exhibited by the Royal Academy, and the British Institution has, this year, followed its example, and has effectually excluded me by this Resolution.
/journal/the-exhibition/.title: A Descriptive Catalogue

/journal/the-last-day/.description: He died on a Sunday evening, singing.
/journal/the-last-day/.preview: On this day, the twelfth of August 1827, William Blake died at his lodgings in Fountain Court, Strand, at the age of sixty-nine.
/journal/the-last-day/.title: The Last Day
